question.text: Mr. Vikram Shetty, Fund Manager at Himalaya Cat III AIF, is explaining to a new LP why NIFTY 50 weights differ from those of a pure market-cap weighted index. Per Box 10.2 of Chapter 10, which of the following shareholdings is typically EXCLUDED while computing free-float market capitalisation?

answer.text: Shares held by retail individual public investors via demat accounts.
Shares held by Mutual Funds under their equity schemes.
Shares held by founders / promoters / controlling shareholders / Government as promoter, and locked-in shares.
Shares held by Foreign Portfolio Investors under the portfolio route.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Box 10.2, free-float EXCLUDES: (i) founders/directors/acquirers with control, (ii) persons with controlling interest, (iii) Government as promoter, (iv) FDI route holdings, (v) strategic stakes by corporates/individuals, (vi) cross-holdings by associates, (vii) Employee Welfare Trusts, (viii) locked-in shares. Retail, MF, and FPI (portfolio route) holdings ARE counted as free-float. The Trap: Option D is the classic trap — FPI via the FDI route is excluded, but FPI via the PORTFOLIO route is included. The candidate must distinguish the two foreign routes. Options A and B represent genuine free-float and are never excluded. Cross-Exam Context: VIII (Equity Derivatives) uses free-float for index-derivative weightings. XIX-A (Distributor) covers free-float at a surface level for investor conversations. Manager's Pro-Tip: When benchmarking a concentrated long-only Cat III AIF versus NIFTY 50 free-float, your active share versus the free-float index will mechanically differ from active share versus full-cap. Report BOTH to sophisticated LPs — it avoids the 'are you really active?' objection.
